{"entries":[{"name_han":"...","logic_thesis":"...","logic_chain":"...","logic_practice":"...","logic_compare":"..."}]}{
  "entries": [
    {
      "name_han": "元始上真眾仙記",
      "logic_thesis": "The text proves that immortal rank is not arbitrary legend but a necessary cosmological order rooted in one primordial source (元始天王 as the personified Dao/Pangu). Only by locating every deity within a single generative hierarchy can fragmented cults claim universal legitimacy against rival revelations.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Chaos precedes form; a first pure essence must already exist within the cosmic egg. 2) That essence self-names as Yuanshi Tianwang and opens heaven-earth; therefore all later gods are derivatives, not peers. 3) Derivative beings receive graded palaces (Yujing upper/middle/lower) proportional to their proximity to the root. 4) Human aspirants inherit this same graded logic: without knowing the root and seat-order, study of scattered immortal records remains incomplete. 5) Conclusion: a complete immortal register is the epistemological condition for true longevity practice.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Map a natal BaZi chart against cosmic hierarchy: Day Master as local 'officer,' Ten Gods as court functionaries under a single Dao-source. 2) When reading deities or star-lords, always ask 'who generates whom' rather than collecting names. 3) Use the text's '极妙之根' criterion to reject unrooted folk talismans. 4) In meditation, orient the upper palace (Yuanshi) as the still axis before invoking secondary gods. 5) Treat lineage charts (師承) as functional analogues of the immortal register.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike Tao Hongjing's later 真靈位業圖, which administratively ranks spirits like a bureaucracy, this work argues cosmogonic necessity first and rank second. It also differs from pure Laozi-centric northern theology by relocating the root from historical sage to pre-cosmic Yuanshi, precisely to unify southern Shangqing pantheons under one origin."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "赤松子中誡經",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that unequal wealth, rank, and lifespan are not arbitrary fate or pure ancestral luck, but the measurable overlay of good or evil qi produced by conduct. Moral action is therefore a physical-causal technology that recruits spiritual protection or invites disaster.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Empirical premise: people born under the same sky live radically unequal lives. 2) If Heaven were purely random or purely hereditary, moral teaching would be useless; yet sages teach morality. 3) Therefore inequality must track an intervening causal medium—善氣/凶氣 generated by deeds. 4) Good qi covers a person → deities guard; evil qi covers → calamity follows (氣→報). 5) Conclusion: longevity and fortune are partly engineered by sustained ethical qi-hygiene, not only natal endowment.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Read BaZi 'good/bad luck periods' as qi-overlays modifiable by conduct, not fixed scripts. 2) Track daily deeds as 氣 accumulation: deceit thickens 凶氣; fidelity thickens 善氣. 3) When chart shows weak Resource/Officer, prioritize ethical repair before talismanic fixes. 4) Use confession-and-amendment cycles (like the text's warnings) before major luck-shift years. 5) Treat '神靈衛之' as a working hypothesis: stable virtue lowers volatility of misfortune.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike purely calendrical fate books that freeze destiny at birth, this text inserts a continuous moral feedback loop. Unlike Buddhist karma framed as mental continuity across rebirths, it frames retribution as present-life qi physics—closer to Han yin-yang resonance than to Indian soteriology."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太清五十八願文",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that salvation efficacy is not only private alchemy or external rite, but is generated by the vow-power (願) of a cultivated intention that binds the practitioner to cosmic and social liberation. Vow is a causal engine: without formalized aspiration, technique lacks vector.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Beings suffer because their intention is fragmented and self-centered. 2) A complete path must reverse that fragmentation by publicly structured aspirations. 3) Fifty-eight vows systematically cover self, others, cosmos, and posthumous states—closing loopholes of partial compassion. 4) Once vowed, action and rite become expressions of a fixed vector rather than sporadic merit. 5) Conclusion: liberation scales with the completeness and sincerity of vow, not merely with technical skill.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Before chart consultation or ritual, state a precise 願 (whom to benefit, what to correct). 2) Convert vague wishes ('good luck') into numbered, checkable vows. 3) Align vows with weak chart sectors (e.g., vow service when Officer is weak). 4) Re-read vows at season turns as 四時 renewal. 5) Treat broken vows as qi-leakage requiring reparation before new cultivation.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike pure precept texts (戒) that prohibit, this text affirms directional aspiration. Unlike Buddhist bodhisattva vows it imitates in form, its frame remains Lingbao-Daoist: vows operate within 度人 cosmology and Taiqing hierarchy, not emptiness doctrine. It is more intentional than 赤松子's passive qi-retribution model."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "黃籙破獄燈儀",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that underworld suffering is ontologically a deficit of yang-light; therefore lamp-ritual is not mere symbolism but a transfer of solar/celestial 陽炁 that opens prisons and re-educates yin souls. Light is soteriological physics under Huanglu covenant.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Above the nine heavens yin dissolves; below the nine earths yang is sealed—hence long night. 2) Souls sink because they lack illuminating yang, not only because of legal sentence. 3) Ritual lamps instantiate 九幽神燈 / multi-lamp arrays as portable suns. 4) Coupled with Huanglu merit and tianzun invocation, light reopens paths of rebirth. 5) Conclusion: breaking hell is primarily re-illumination, secondarily legal petition.",
      "logic_practice": "1) For ancestral BaZi or death-year analysis, diagnose 'yin excess' as darkness needing light practices, not only curse-breaking. 2) Use lamp count and directions as analogues of stem-branch fire balance. 3) Pair lighting with confession of the deceased's chart flaws (greed, rage) to match light with moral heat. 4) In personal cultivation, evening lamp meditation to counter kidney-water excess. 5) Never treat破獄 as private revenge magic; keep the text's universal-degree intent.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike talisman-only破獄 that relies on seal authority, this instrument prioritizes optical-yang technology. Unlike 靈寶施食法, which nourishes through food, this nourishes through light. Later internalist readings (身中九獄) go further by locating hells in the body—this lamp text remains primarily liturgical-external."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "碧虛子親傳直指",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that the sole true elixir base is the prenatal One Qi (先天一氣), and that bookish Nanzong study without living oral transmission collapses into dead words. Direct pointing after long seeking is the epistemic form of the Dao itself.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Canonical danjing and songs are necessary but insufficient—the author exhausts them and still lacks the key. 2) Wandering and comparing teachers shows partial methods diverge. 3) Encounter with Haiqiong (Bai Yuchan) supplies the missing seal: 先天一氣 as sole base. 4) Therefore all post-natal forced firing without prenatal recovery is branch, not root. 5) Conclusion: authentic method is short, oral, and mind-to-mind; multiplication of techniques signals error.",
      "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi, privilege Day Master and prenatal chart structure (year-month as 'congenital') before decade luck micro-management. 2) Reduce technique clutter: one principal method, verified. 3) Seek living correction (師印) after self-study, not instead of it. 4) Use '直指' criterion: if a method cannot be stated simply, suspect ornament. 5) Journal only changes in 炁 sensation, not literary elegance.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 玉谿子丹經指要, which systematizes and charts the whole school, this text weaponizes brevity and personal encounter narrative. Unlike northern Quanzhen pure stillness texts, it remains Nanzong fire-phasing oriented but insists the fire is empty without prenatal recovery."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "玉谿子丹經指要",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that gold-fire reversion (金火還返) must be sought only inside one body, and that lineage coherence (混元宗派) is the filter against spurious external and dual-cult paths. Systematization is itself a form of protection of the Dao.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Scattered danjing generate contradictory procedures. 2) Li Jianyi reconstructs a single Nanzong spine from Zhang Boduan onward. 3) The core inference: true work is internal reversion of metal and fire; outside the body is non-Dao. 4) School chart (宗派圖) operationalizes who may authorize whom. 5) Conclusion: orthodoxy equals internal locus plus verified transmission, not antiquity of a title alone.",
      "logic_practice": "1) When chart shows strong external '財' chasing, reframe practice as return (還返), not acquisition. 2) Use the text's rejection of 身外 to discard room-temperature alchemy promises. 3) Build a personal '宗派圖' of teachers/books actually used—prune orphans. 4) Sequence: stabilize form → gather 炁 → apply fire phases, not reverse. 5) Cross-check any new technique against 'is it inside one body?'",
      "logic_compare": "More taxonomic and pedagogically complete than 碧虛子's intimate直指; less purely philosophical than 峴泉集. Differs from Zhong-Lü longevity poetry by inserting explicit school genealogy as a truth-condition."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "穆天子傳",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that the sacred West (Kunlun/Yaochi) is a reachable geopolitical-ritual horizon: royal mobility, tribute, and banquet can contact the divine without yet requiring full Daoist interior transformation. Immortality here is spatial-political, not primarily alchemical.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Zhou Mu travels beyond ordinary borders through logistical power. 2) He reaches Yaochi and banquets with Xiwangmu as peer-exchange, not pure supplication. 3) Songs and gifts encode life-death and kingship messages. 4) Return does not equal permanent transcendence—contact is temporary. 5) Conclusion: sacred space is accessible to sovereign virtue and movement, but the text does not prove irreversible immortality.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Read 'travel to the West' as metaphor for moving chart luck toward Resource/Seal sectors. 2) Treat ritual banquet (offerings, music, timing) as diplomatic protocol with spirits. 3) Map Kunlun as the chart's extreme Resource pole—approach with order, not greed. 4) Use seasonal touring/retreats as mild analogues of Mu's circuit. 5) Remember: contact ≠ completion; avoid mistaking peak experience for consolidation.",
      "logic_compare": "Pre-Daoist and archival compared with 漢武帝內傳, which converts the same Xiwangmu motif into a failed-disciple cautionary tale. Unlike pure mythic 山海經 taxonomy, Mu Tianzi presents itinerary realism—distance, logistics, protocol—as the logic of sacred encounter."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "漢武帝內傳",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that imperial power, offerings, and even face-to-face divine descent cannot confer immortality without 仙才, secrecy, and disciplined receptivity. The emperor's failure is the proof that technique is graded and character-gated.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Emperor desires longevity and receives Xiwangmu and Shangyuan Furen. 2) He is granted peaches, teachings, and the twelve 靈飛 methods under strict conditions. 3) He fails secrecy/discipline; judgment: '非仙才'. 4) Therefore transmission success tracks fitness, not rank or wealth. 5) Conclusion: the highest scriptures are self-protecting—unready holders lose them.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Before advanced BaZi or neidan methods, audit 仙才 proxies: patience, secrecy, non-instrumental motive. 2) Keep oral keys out of public performance. 3) Treat 'received but not kept' as a chart pattern (strong Wealth, weak Seal). 4) Practice graded unlocks: foundational purity before 六甲-level complexity. 5) Use the emperor as negative case study against consumerist spirituality.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 穆天子傳's largely successful royal embassy, this text dramatizes pedagogical failure. Unlike 元始上真眾仙記's register of already-immortals, it focuses on the gate conditions of entry. It is more Shangqing-talismanic than Mu's archaic banquet diplomacy."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "洞玄靈寶玄門大義",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that the Daoist 'mysterious gate' is a coherent doctrinal system—cosmology, scriptures, causation, and salvation—not a heap of spells. Lingbao identity is established by integrated 大義 (great meaning), which legitimates practice.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Competing rites without shared metaphysics breed confusion. 2) The text articulates core Xuanmen categories (Dao, scriptures, ranks, retribution, salvation). 3) Each category implies the others: no 度人 without cosmology; no cosmology without scriptural vehicle. 4) Therefore orthodoxy is conceptual coherence under Lingbao frame. 5) Conclusion: correct meaning precedes effective method.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Before adopting a ritual, write its doctrinal premise in one paragraph. 2) Align BaZi counseling with explicit 因果 language rather than pure luckism. 3) Use the text as a checklist: does a practice serve 度人 and return to Dao? 4) Teach clients a mini-大義 before selling techniques. 5) Reject methods that cannot state their place in the system.",
      "logic_compare": "More abstract and definitional than 道學科儀, which operationalizes training steps. Less pantheon-narrative than 元始上真眾仙記. It is the 'constitution' text relative to later detailed liturgies."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "洞玄靈寶道學科儀",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that the Dao is learned through regulated curriculum and ritual discipline (科儀), not spontaneous inspiration alone. Orthopraxy forms the body-mind into a vessel capable of receiving higher teachings.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Aspiration without training produces chaos and false masters. 2) Codified stages of study, deportment, and rite shape the student. 3) Each 科 item is both ethical and technical: how one stands, recites, and serves is already practice. 4) Graduated discipline yields reliable transmission capacity. 5) Conclusion: institutional method is a spiritual technology, not a bureaucratic accident.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Design a personal daily 科 (sleep, diet, recitation, sitting) as non-negotiable. 2) In BaZi work, treat weak Earth/Seal as need for more ritual structure. 3) Sequence learning: deportment → scripture → rite → higher method. 4) Use communal liturgy periodically to correct solitary drift. 5) Measure progress by reliability of form, not only peak states.",
      "logic_compare": "Where 玄門大義 defines meaning, this text engineers habitus. Unlike pure neidan '直指' works that minimize outer form, it insists form is the path. Closer to monastic rule than to court lamp spectacles."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "北帝七元紫庭延生祕訣",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that lifespan and epidemic fate can be renegotiated by aligning the body with Beidi's demon-subduing authority and the Seven Yuan star-lords. Longevity is astral-military: protect the life-court (紫庭) by summoning correct stellar officers.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Premature death and plague are read as invasions of disordered spirits. 2) Beidi governs the north and coercive rectification; Seven Yuan govern temporal cycles. 3) Talismans, true-form diagrams, and invocations couple human life to these offices. 4) Proper alignment yields 延生 and 集福. 5) Conclusion: life extension is jurisdictional petition plus star-body resonance, not only herbal medicine.",
      "logic_practice": "1) For short-life BaZi patterns, emphasize northern Water regulation and Officer/Authority balance. 2) Time protective rites to Big Dipper phases and personal destiny stars. 3) Combine medical hygiene with star-talisman logic rather than replacing either. 4) Visualize 紫庭 as chest-heart court kept clear of chaotic thoughts (inner 'epidemics'). 5) Use seven-lamp or seven-day sequences as micro-models of 七元.",
      "logic_compare": "More martial-astral than pure 養生錄 dietetics; more stellar than 黃籙 lamp hell-breaking. Unlike Zhengyi covenant texts focused on communal orthodoxy, this prioritizes individual lifespan defense under Beidi."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "正一天師告趙昇口訣",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that Zhengyi Mengwei Dao arises as a corrective response to the 'incorrect Six Heavens': cosmic disorder requires a new covenant, seals, and disciple discipline. Orthodoxy is historical emergency legislation from the Most High through Zhang Daoling.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Premise: prior celestial administration (六天) is corrupt/incorrect. 2) Laojun therefore bestows 正一盟威 on Zhang. 3) Zhang transmits orally to Zhao Sheng with seals/符 (e.g., five sprouts). 4) Correct practice restores cosmic and communal order. 5) Conclusion: legitimacy of method depends on covenant continuity and correction of disorder, not novelty.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Frame BaZi 'killing' or chaotic patterns as 六天-style disorder needing 正一 rectification (clear rules, honest speech). 2) Prefer methods with clear lineage seals over anonymous spells. 3) Use oral-key ethics: no selling of what was given under vow. 4) Practice five-sprout / five-phase nourishment as body-level covenant. 5) Community integrity as part of personal cultivation.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike Lingbao 度人 universalism, this is covenant-sectarian and historically pointed. Unlike 碧虛子 neidan intimacy, authority is institutional-charismatic. It explains why Zhengyi privileges register, talisman, and oath."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太上洞神行道授度儀",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that the right to 'walk the Dao' (行道) is conferred by formal ordination liturgy, not by private claim. Dongshen grade authority is performatively created through 授度 protocol—rank is ritual fact.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Without public transmission, anyone could invent authority. 2) 授度儀 scripts witnesses, texts, vows, and deity invitation. 3) Completing the script transforms candidate status. 4) Post-ordination practice is then accountable to that status. 5) Conclusion: ritual form is the ontology of religious office.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Treat major life transitions (luck decade changes) as personal 授度: rite + vow + new rule set. 2) Do not practice higher registers without corresponding ethical grade. 3) Document initiations (teachers, dates) like a liturgical archive. 4) Use the text's solemnity against casual online 'empowerments'. 5) Rehearse posture and speech as part of 行道, not ornament.",
      "logic_compare": "More about conferring status than 黃籙破獄's saving the dead, and more legal-performative than 道學科儀's ongoing student discipline. Differs from pure lineage storytelling by making the ceremony itself the causal engine of authority."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "峴泉集",
      "logic_thesis": "Zhang Yuchu proves that institutional Daoism (Zhengyi leadership, canon, morality) and classical philosophical Dao must be re-fused: without literary-intellectual reform, ritual apparatus decays; without institutional order, pure talk of Dao is sterile.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Late Yuan–early Ming Daoism suffers textual disorder and moral laxity. 2) As Celestial Master, Zhang writes essays uniting Laozi-Zhuangzi insight with liturgical responsibility. 3) Reform of persons and of offices are one project. 4) Therefore elite letters serve soteriology and governance together. 5) Conclusion: the healthy Dao is simultaneously metaphysical, ethical, and administrative.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Pair any practical method with a short philosophical self-audit (名/利/欲). 2) In BaZi counseling, address character structure, not only date picking. 3) Curate a personal 'canon' of few deep texts over many shallow ones. 4) Practice institutional virtues: reliability, record-keeping, non-exploitation of clients. 5) Write reflective notes (as Zhang does) to clarify teaching.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike single-method neidan tracts, it is a polymath reform corpus. Unlike early revelation texts, its authority is historical office plus erudition. It stands opposite pure anti-institutional hermit ideals while still defending inner purity."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "靈寶施食法",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that hungry, wandering yin beings are transformed primarily through ritualized food and mantra-powered offering: nourishment is the medium of 度人. Compassion must be metabolized into edible merit.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Premature and neglected dead suffer hunger—literally deficient posthumous qi. 2) Ordinary food cannot reach them; consecrated food can. 3) Lingbao method multiplies and spiritualizes offerings via spell, mudra, and visualization. 4) Fed souls cool grievance and open rebirth paths. 5) Conclusion: soteriology works through alimentary transformation, not light or law alone.",
      "logic_practice": "1) For ancestral hardship years in BaZi, schedule 施食 or equivalent offerings. 2) Eat with mindful dedication (first portion mentally offered). 3) Balance personal diet as mirror of feeding practice—no waste. 4) Use sweet/clear foods as symbolic yang for yin ghosts. 5) Combine with confession of family pattern (greed, neglect) to match food with meaning.",
      "logic_compare": "Complements 黃籙破獄燈儀 (light) with food; more concrete than abstract 願文. Differs from Buddhist 瑜伽焰口 in staying within Lingbao cosmology and Daoist liturgical grammar, though structurally related."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "混俗頤生錄",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that true nourishing of life (頤生) is compatible with remaining in the secular world: hygiene, moderation, and mild practices outperform total flight from society for most people. Integration is higher skill than pure escape.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Many fail because they equate cultivation with renunciation they cannot sustain. 2) Body and mind are damaged more by disorderly secular habits than by society itself. 3) Regulated diet, sleep, sex, emotion, and light exercises restore balance amid duties. 4) Sustainable mild method beats heroic short method. 5) Conclusion: 混俗 is not compromise of Dao but its realistic vector.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Design BaZi-based lifestyle rules that fit career/family constraints. 2) Fix sleep and meal timing before advanced meditation. 3) Convert chart warnings into daily micro-habits (e.g., weak Water → earlier rest). 4) Practice 'hidden cultivation'—invisible to colleagues. 5) Review monthly: what secular friction is still leaking jing?",
      "logic_compare": "Opposed to pure mountain-hermit ideals and to high-ritual clerical paths. More pragmatic than 修真祕錄's secret perfection rhetoric; closer to literati self-care than to Beidi martial longevity."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "保生要錄",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that life is preserved by early, essential, preventive measures—guarding essence before disease manifests. The 'essential record' logic: few high-leverage rules beat complex late treatment.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Illness and short life follow long unnoticed leakage of jing-qi. 2) Medical-Daoist essentials target sleep, diet, emotion, and seasonal care. 3) Acting at the 'not-yet' stage multiplies efficacy. 4) Over-medication and over-technique after collapse are inferior. 5) Conclusion: preservation (保) is temporally prior and logically superior to rescue.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Annual BaZi health forecast → preventive regimen, not crisis magic. 2) Identify chart's leakage channel (sex, speech, anger, overwork) and close it. 3) Keep a short '要' list (5 rules max) rather than a thick manual. 4) At each season pivot, reassert essentials. 5) Treat minor symptoms as early-warning 符.",
      "logic_compare": "More minimalist and preventive than encyclopedic yangsheng collections. Less cosmological than 四氣攝生圖, more clinical-practical. Differs from 種芝草法 by focusing on behavior rather than sacred materia."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "修真祕錄",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that 'cultivating perfection' is a secret sequential craft: without ordered steps and concealed keys, scattered longevity tips never cohere into 真. Secrecy protects sequence integrity.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Public miscellaneous tips create false confidence. 2) True work requires staged refinement of body, breath, and spirit. 3) Secrets encode timing, dosage, and contraindications. 4) Wrong order converts medicine to poison. 5) Conclusion: perfection is an engineered process under restricted transmission.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Build a staged curriculum (form → breath → spirit) with clear gates. 2) Hide advanced fire phases until lower gates stabilize. 3) Use BaZi to time stage transitions (e.g., strong Fire years for cautious firing). 4) Keep a private practice log—the modern 祕錄. 5) Test one variable at a time.",
      "logic_compare": "More sequential-esoteric than 混俗頤生錄's open lifestyle advice; less single-pointed than 碧虛子直指. Bridges medical yangsheng and full neidan without being pure liturgy."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "四氣攝生圖",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that health is the art of following the four seasonal qi: each season has a lawful pattern of rise-store-kill-collect, and diagram-mediated knowledge makes that law actionable. Adaptation, not fixed routine, is the method.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Heaven's qi cycles through spring growth, summer flourish, autumn harvest, winter storage. 2) Human body is a microcosm; resisting season creates disease. 3) Diagrams encode clothing, diet, emotion, and exercise per season. 4) Correct seasonal alignment is already 攝生. 5) Conclusion: time-structured living is the primary medicine.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Overlay BaZi month-branch seasons on personal regimen. 2) Spring: move liver-wood (stretch, less anger); winter: store (sleep, less revelation of plans). 3) Use the '圖' idea: one-page seasonal checklist on the wall. 4) Adjust meditation length/heat by season. 5) Read decade luck as a 'long season' and adapt ambition accordingly.",
      "logic_compare": "More calendrical-visual than 保生要錄's essential rules, and more secular-medical than stellar 北帝七元 texts. Differs from pure Five-Phase abstract theory by insisting on illustrated, embodied seasonal tactics."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "種芝草法",
      "logic_thesis": "It proves that sacred longevity substances (靈芝) are not only heaven-sent rarities but can be cultivated by correct method—time, terrain, soil, and ritual care. Immortality materia is partly agricultural technology under numinous signs.",
      "logic_chain": "1) Classical longevity lore prizes zhi as condensed auspicious qi. 2) If zhi were purely miraculous, practice would reduce to waiting. 3) Cultivation methods specify conditions that invite zhi growth. 4) Successful growth demonstrates human-heaven cooperation in producing medicine. 5) Conclusion: outer sacred agriculture is a legitimate branch of the path to long life.",
      "logic_practice": "1) Treat garden/herb work as cultivation of Resource star in BaZi. 2) Align planting and harvest with sexagenary and seasonal qi. 3) Approach materia with purity rules (timing, intention) not only botany. 4) Use 'growing zhi' as metaphor: grow virtues slowly under right conditions. 5) Prefer self-tended simple herbs over exotic untraceable 'immortal drugs'.",
      "logic_compare": "Opposite of pure inner 先天一氣 schools that reject outer drugs; more concrete than abstract 願文. Unlike imperial 漢武帝內傳's ready-made peaches of the goddess, this text democratizes the sacred plant through technique—agriculture as minor alchemy."
    }
  ]
}

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that immortal rank is not arbitrary legend but a necessary cosmological order rooted in one primordial source (元始天王 as the personified Dao/Pangu). Only by locating every deity within a single generative hierarchy can fragmented cults claim universal legitimacy against rival revelations.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Chaos precedes form; a first pure essence must already exist within the cosmic egg. 2) That essence self-names as Yuanshi Tianwang and opens heaven-earth; therefore all later gods are derivatives, not peers. 3) Derivative beings receive graded palaces (Yujing upper/middle/lower) proportional to their proximity to the root. 4) Human aspirants inherit this same graded logic: without knowing the root and seat-order, study of scattered immortal records remains incomplete. 5) Conclusion: a complete immortal register is the epistemological condition for true longevity practice.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map a natal BaZi chart against cosmic hierarchy: Day Master as local 'officer,' Ten Gods as court functionaries under a single Dao-source. 2) When reading deities or star-lords, always ask 'who generates whom' rather than collecting names. 3) Use the text's '极妙之根' criterion to reject unrooted folk talismans. 4) In meditation, orient the upper palace (Yuanshi) as the still axis before invoking secondary gods. 5) Treat lineage charts (師承) as functional analogues of the immortal register.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Tao Hongjing's later 真靈位業圖, which administratively ranks spirits like a bureaucracy, this work argues cosmogonic necessity first and rank second. It also differs from pure Laozi-centric northern theology by relocating the root from historical sage to pre-cosmic Yuanshi, precisely to unify southern Shangqing pantheons under one origin.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that unequal wealth, rank, and lifespan are not arbitrary fate or pure ancestral luck, but the measurable overlay of good or evil qi produced by conduct. Moral action is therefore a physical-causal technology that recruits spiritual protection or invites disaster.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Empirical premise: people born under the same sky live radically unequal lives. 2) If Heaven were purely random or purely hereditary, moral teaching would be useless; yet sages teach morality. 3) Therefore inequality must track an intervening causal medium—善氣/凶氣 generated by deeds. 4) Good qi covers a person → deities guard; evil qi covers → calamity follows (氣→報). 5) Conclusion: longevity and fortune are partly engineered by sustained ethical qi-hygiene, not only natal endowment.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read BaZi 'good/bad luck periods' as qi-overlays modifiable by conduct, not fixed scripts. 2) Track daily deeds as 氣 accumulation: deceit thickens 凶氣; fidelity thickens 善氣. 3) When chart shows weak Resource/Officer, prioritize ethical repair before talismanic fixes. 4) Use confession-and-amendment cycles (like the text's warnings) before major luck-shift years. 5) Treat '神靈衛之' as a working hypothesis: stable virtue lowers volatility of misfortune.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike purely calendrical fate books that freeze destiny at birth, this text inserts a continuous moral feedback loop. Unlike Buddhist karma framed as mental continuity across rebirths, it frames retribution as present-life qi physics—closer to Han yin-yang resonance than to Indian soteriology.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that salvation efficacy is not only private alchemy or external rite, but is generated by the vow-power (願) of a cultivated intention that binds the practitioner to cosmic and social liberation. Vow is a causal engine: without formalized aspiration, technique lacks vector.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Beings suffer because their intention is fragmented and self-centered. 2) A complete path must reverse that fragmentation by publicly structured aspirations. 3) Fifty-eight vows systematically cover self, others, cosmos, and posthumous states—closing loopholes of partial compassion. 4) Once vowed, action and rite become expressions of a fixed vector rather than sporadic merit. 5) Conclusion: liberation scales with the completeness and sincerity of vow, not merely with technical skill.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before chart consultation or ritual, state a precise 願 (whom to benefit, what to correct). 2) Convert vague wishes ('good luck') into numbered, checkable vows. 3) Align vows with weak chart sectors (e.g., vow service when Officer is weak). 4) Re-read vows at season turns as 四時 renewal. 5) Treat broken vows as qi-leakage requiring reparation before new cultivation.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure precept texts (戒) that prohibit, this text affirms directional aspiration. Unlike Buddhist bodhisattva vows it imitates in form, its frame remains Lingbao-Daoist: vows operate within 度人 cosmology and Taiqing hierarchy, not emptiness doctrine. It is more intentional than 赤松子's passive qi-retribution model.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that underworld suffering is ontologically a deficit of yang-light; therefore lamp-ritual is not mere symbolism but a transfer of solar/celestial 陽炁 that opens prisons and re-educates yin souls. Light is soteriological physics under Huanglu covenant.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Above the nine heavens yin dissolves; below the nine earths yang is sealed—hence long night. 2) Souls sink because they lack illuminating yang, not only because of legal sentence. 3) Ritual lamps instantiate 九幽神燈 / multi-lamp arrays as portable suns. 4) Coupled with Huanglu merit and tianzun invocation, light reopens paths of rebirth. 5) Conclusion: breaking hell is primarily re-illumination, secondarily legal petition.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For ancestral BaZi or death-year analysis, diagnose 'yin excess' as darkness needing light practices, not only curse-breaking. 2) Use lamp count and directions as analogues of stem-branch fire balance. 3) Pair lighting with confession of the deceased's chart flaws (greed, rage) to match light with moral heat. 4) In personal cultivation, evening lamp meditation to counter kidney-water excess. 5) Never treat破獄 as private revenge magic; keep the text's universal-degree intent.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike talisman-only破獄 that relies on seal authority, this instrument prioritizes optical-yang technology. Unlike 靈寶施食法, which nourishes through food, this nourishes through light. Later internalist readings (身中九獄) go further by locating hells in the body—this lamp text remains primarily liturgical-external.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the sole true elixir base is the prenatal One Qi (先天一氣), and that bookish Nanzong study without living oral transmission collapses into dead words. Direct pointing after long seeking is the epistemic form of the Dao itself.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Canonical danjing and songs are necessary but insufficient—the author exhausts them and still lacks the key. 2) Wandering and comparing teachers shows partial methods diverge. 3) Encounter with Haiqiong (Bai Yuchan) supplies the missing seal: 先天一氣 as sole base. 4) Therefore all post-natal forced firing without prenatal recovery is branch, not root. 5) Conclusion: authentic method is short, oral, and mind-to-mind; multiplication of techniques signals error.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, privilege Day Master and prenatal chart structure (year-month as 'congenital') before decade luck micro-management. 2) Reduce technique clutter: one principal method, verified. 3) Seek living correction (師印) after self-study, not instead of it. 4) Use '直指' criterion: if a method cannot be stated simply, suspect ornament. 5) Journal only changes in 炁 sensation, not literary elegance.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 玉谿子丹經指要, which systematizes and charts the whole school, this text weaponizes brevity and personal encounter narrative. Unlike northern Quanzhen pure stillness texts, it remains Nanzong fire-phasing oriented but insists the fire is empty without prenatal recovery.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that gold-fire reversion (金火還返) must be sought only inside one body, and that lineage coherence (混元宗派) is the filter against spurious external and dual-cult paths. Systematization is itself a form of protection of the Dao.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Scattered danjing generate contradictory procedures. 2) Li Jianyi reconstructs a single Nanzong spine from Zhang Boduan onward. 3) The core inference: true work is internal reversion of metal and fire; outside the body is non-Dao. 4) School chart (宗派圖) operationalizes who may authorize whom. 5) Conclusion: orthodoxy equals internal locus plus verified transmission, not antiquity of a title alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When chart shows strong external '財' chasing, reframe practice as return (還返), not acquisition. 2) Use the text's rejection of 身外 to discard room-temperature alchemy promises. 3) Build a personal '宗派圖' of teachers/books actually used—prune orphans. 4) Sequence: stabilize form → gather 炁 → apply fire phases, not reverse. 5) Cross-check any new technique against 'is it inside one body?'
entries.logic_compare: More taxonomic and pedagogically complete than 碧虛子's intimate直指; less purely philosophical than 峴泉集. Differs from Zhong-Lü longevity poetry by inserting explicit school genealogy as a truth-condition.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the sacred West (Kunlun/Yaochi) is a reachable geopolitical-ritual horizon: royal mobility, tribute, and banquet can contact the divine without yet requiring full Daoist interior transformation. Immortality here is spatial-political, not primarily alchemical.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Zhou Mu travels beyond ordinary borders through logistical power. 2) He reaches Yaochi and banquets with Xiwangmu as peer-exchange, not pure supplication. 3) Songs and gifts encode life-death and kingship messages. 4) Return does not equal permanent transcendence—contact is temporary. 5) Conclusion: sacred space is accessible to sovereign virtue and movement, but the text does not prove irreversible immortality.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read 'travel to the West' as metaphor for moving chart luck toward Resource/Seal sectors. 2) Treat ritual banquet (offerings, music, timing) as diplomatic protocol with spirits. 3) Map Kunlun as the chart's extreme Resource pole—approach with order, not greed. 4) Use seasonal touring/retreats as mild analogues of Mu's circuit. 5) Remember: contact ≠ completion; avoid mistaking peak experience for consolidation.
entries.logic_compare: Pre-Daoist and archival compared with 漢武帝內傳, which converts the same Xiwangmu motif into a failed-disciple cautionary tale. Unlike pure mythic 山海經 taxonomy, Mu Tianzi presents itinerary realism—distance, logistics, protocol—as the logic of sacred encounter.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that imperial power, offerings, and even face-to-face divine descent cannot confer immortality without 仙才, secrecy, and disciplined receptivity. The emperor's failure is the proof that technique is graded and character-gated.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Emperor desires longevity and receives Xiwangmu and Shangyuan Furen. 2) He is granted peaches, teachings, and the twelve 靈飛 methods under strict conditions. 3) He fails secrecy/discipline; judgment: '非仙才'. 4) Therefore transmission success tracks fitness, not rank or wealth. 5) Conclusion: the highest scriptures are self-protecting—unready holders lose them.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before advanced BaZi or neidan methods, audit 仙才 proxies: patience, secrecy, non-instrumental motive. 2) Keep oral keys out of public performance. 3) Treat 'received but not kept' as a chart pattern (strong Wealth, weak Seal). 4) Practice graded unlocks: foundational purity before 六甲-level complexity. 5) Use the emperor as negative case study against consumerist spirituality.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 穆天子傳's largely successful royal embassy, this text dramatizes pedagogical failure. Unlike 元始上真眾仙記's register of already-immortals, it focuses on the gate conditions of entry. It is more Shangqing-talismanic than Mu's archaic banquet diplomacy.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the Daoist 'mysterious gate' is a coherent doctrinal system—cosmology, scriptures, causation, and salvation—not a heap of spells. Lingbao identity is established by integrated 大義 (great meaning), which legitimates practice.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Competing rites without shared metaphysics breed confusion. 2) The text articulates core Xuanmen categories (Dao, scriptures, ranks, retribution, salvation). 3) Each category implies the others: no 度人 without cosmology; no cosmology without scriptural vehicle. 4) Therefore orthodoxy is conceptual coherence under Lingbao frame. 5) Conclusion: correct meaning precedes effective method.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before adopting a ritual, write its doctrinal premise in one paragraph. 2) Align BaZi counseling with explicit 因果 language rather than pure luckism. 3) Use the text as a checklist: does a practice serve 度人 and return to Dao? 4) Teach clients a mini-大義 before selling techniques. 5) Reject methods that cannot state their place in the system.
entries.logic_compare: More abstract and definitional than 道學科儀, which operationalizes training steps. Less pantheon-narrative than 元始上真眾仙記. It is the 'constitution' text relative to later detailed liturgies.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the Dao is learned through regulated curriculum and ritual discipline (科儀), not spontaneous inspiration alone. Orthopraxy forms the body-mind into a vessel capable of receiving higher teachings.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Aspiration without training produces chaos and false masters. 2) Codified stages of study, deportment, and rite shape the student. 3) Each 科 item is both ethical and technical: how one stands, recites, and serves is already practice. 4) Graduated discipline yields reliable transmission capacity. 5) Conclusion: institutional method is a spiritual technology, not a bureaucratic accident.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Design a personal daily 科 (sleep, diet, recitation, sitting) as non-negotiable. 2) In BaZi work, treat weak Earth/Seal as need for more ritual structure. 3) Sequence learning: deportment → scripture → rite → higher method. 4) Use communal liturgy periodically to correct solitary drift. 5) Measure progress by reliability of form, not only peak states.
entries.logic_compare: Where 玄門大義 defines meaning, this text engineers habitus. Unlike pure neidan '直指' works that minimize outer form, it insists form is the path. Closer to monastic rule than to court lamp spectacles.

entries.name_han: 北帝七元紫庭延生祕訣
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that lifespan and epidemic fate can be renegotiated by aligning the body with Beidi's demon-subduing authority and the Seven Yuan star-lords. Longevity is astral-military: protect the life-court (紫庭) by summoning correct stellar officers.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premature death and plague are read as invasions of disordered spirits. 2) Beidi governs the north and coercive rectification; Seven Yuan govern temporal cycles. 3) Talismans, true-form diagrams, and invocations couple human life to these offices. 4) Proper alignment yields 延生 and 集福. 5) Conclusion: life extension is jurisdictional petition plus star-body resonance, not only herbal medicine.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For short-life BaZi patterns, emphasize northern Water regulation and Officer/Authority balance. 2) Time protective rites to Big Dipper phases and personal destiny stars. 3) Combine medical hygiene with star-talisman logic rather than replacing either. 4) Visualize 紫庭 as chest-heart court kept clear of chaotic thoughts (inner 'epidemics'). 5) Use seven-lamp or seven-day sequences as micro-models of 七元.
entries.logic_compare: More martial-astral than pure 養生錄 dietetics; more stellar than 黃籙 lamp hell-breaking. Unlike Zhengyi covenant texts focused on communal orthodoxy, this prioritizes individual lifespan defense under Beidi.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Zhengyi Mengwei Dao arises as a corrective response to the 'incorrect Six Heavens': cosmic disorder requires a new covenant, seals, and disciple discipline. Orthodoxy is historical emergency legislation from the Most High through Zhang Daoling.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: prior celestial administration (六天) is corrupt/incorrect. 2) Laojun therefore bestows 正一盟威 on Zhang. 3) Zhang transmits orally to Zhao Sheng with seals/符 (e.g., five sprouts). 4) Correct practice restores cosmic and communal order. 5) Conclusion: legitimacy of method depends on covenant continuity and correction of disorder, not novelty.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Frame BaZi 'killing' or chaotic patterns as 六天-style disorder needing 正一 rectification (clear rules, honest speech). 2) Prefer methods with clear lineage seals over anonymous spells. 3) Use oral-key ethics: no selling of what was given under vow. 4) Practice five-sprout / five-phase nourishment as body-level covenant. 5) Community integrity as part of personal cultivation.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Lingbao 度人 universalism, this is covenant-sectarian and historically pointed. Unlike 碧虛子 neidan intimacy, authority is institutional-charismatic. It explains why Zhengyi privileges register, talisman, and oath.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the right to 'walk the Dao' (行道) is conferred by formal ordination liturgy, not by private claim. Dongshen grade authority is performatively created through 授度 protocol—rank is ritual fact.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Without public transmission, anyone could invent authority. 2) 授度儀 scripts witnesses, texts, vows, and deity invitation. 3) Completing the script transforms candidate status. 4) Post-ordination practice is then accountable to that status. 5) Conclusion: ritual form is the ontology of religious office.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat major life transitions (luck decade changes) as personal 授度: rite + vow + new rule set. 2) Do not practice higher registers without corresponding ethical grade. 3) Document initiations (teachers, dates) like a liturgical archive. 4) Use the text's solemnity against casual online 'empowerments'. 5) Rehearse posture and speech as part of 行道, not ornament.
entries.logic_compare: More about conferring status than 黃籙破獄's saving the dead, and more legal-performative than 道學科儀's ongoing student discipline. Differs from pure lineage storytelling by making the ceremony itself the causal engine of authority.

entries.logic_thesis: Zhang Yuchu proves that institutional Daoism (Zhengyi leadership, canon, morality) and classical philosophical Dao must be re-fused: without literary-intellectual reform, ritual apparatus decays; without institutional order, pure talk of Dao is sterile.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Late Yuan–early Ming Daoism suffers textual disorder and moral laxity. 2) As Celestial Master, Zhang writes essays uniting Laozi-Zhuangzi insight with liturgical responsibility. 3) Reform of persons and of offices are one project. 4) Therefore elite letters serve soteriology and governance together. 5) Conclusion: the healthy Dao is simultaneously metaphysical, ethical, and administrative.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Pair any practical method with a short philosophical self-audit (名/利/欲). 2) In BaZi counseling, address character structure, not only date picking. 3) Curate a personal 'canon' of few deep texts over many shallow ones. 4) Practice institutional virtues: reliability, record-keeping, non-exploitation of clients. 5) Write reflective notes (as Zhang does) to clarify teaching.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike single-method neidan tracts, it is a polymath reform corpus. Unlike early revelation texts, its authority is historical office plus erudition. It stands opposite pure anti-institutional hermit ideals while still defending inner purity.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that hungry, wandering yin beings are transformed primarily through ritualized food and mantra-powered offering: nourishment is the medium of 度人. Compassion must be metabolized into edible merit.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premature and neglected dead suffer hunger—literally deficient posthumous qi. 2) Ordinary food cannot reach them; consecrated food can. 3) Lingbao method multiplies and spiritualizes offerings via spell, mudra, and visualization. 4) Fed souls cool grievance and open rebirth paths. 5) Conclusion: soteriology works through alimentary transformation, not light or law alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For ancestral hardship years in BaZi, schedule 施食 or equivalent offerings. 2) Eat with mindful dedication (first portion mentally offered). 3) Balance personal diet as mirror of feeding practice—no waste. 4) Use sweet/clear foods as symbolic yang for yin ghosts. 5) Combine with confession of family pattern (greed, neglect) to match food with meaning.
entries.logic_compare: Complements 黃籙破獄燈儀 (light) with food; more concrete than abstract 願文. Differs from Buddhist 瑜伽焰口 in staying within Lingbao cosmology and Daoist liturgical grammar, though structurally related.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that true nourishing of life (頤生) is compatible with remaining in the secular world: hygiene, moderation, and mild practices outperform total flight from society for most people. Integration is higher skill than pure escape.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Many fail because they equate cultivation with renunciation they cannot sustain. 2) Body and mind are damaged more by disorderly secular habits than by society itself. 3) Regulated diet, sleep, sex, emotion, and light exercises restore balance amid duties. 4) Sustainable mild method beats heroic short method. 5) Conclusion: 混俗 is not compromise of Dao but its realistic vector.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Design BaZi-based lifestyle rules that fit career/family constraints. 2) Fix sleep and meal timing before advanced meditation. 3) Convert chart warnings into daily micro-habits (e.g., weak Water → earlier rest). 4) Practice 'hidden cultivation'—invisible to colleagues. 5) Review monthly: what secular friction is still leaking jing?
entries.logic_compare: Opposed to pure mountain-hermit ideals and to high-ritual clerical paths. More pragmatic than 修真祕錄's secret perfection rhetoric; closer to literati self-care than to Beidi martial longevity.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that life is preserved by early, essential, preventive measures—guarding essence before disease manifests. The 'essential record' logic: few high-leverage rules beat complex late treatment.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Illness and short life follow long unnoticed leakage of jing-qi. 2) Medical-Daoist essentials target sleep, diet, emotion, and seasonal care. 3) Acting at the 'not-yet' stage multiplies efficacy. 4) Over-medication and over-technique after collapse are inferior. 5) Conclusion: preservation (保) is temporally prior and logically superior to rescue.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Annual BaZi health forecast → preventive regimen, not crisis magic. 2) Identify chart's leakage channel (sex, speech, anger, overwork) and close it. 3) Keep a short '要' list (5 rules max) rather than a thick manual. 4) At each season pivot, reassert essentials. 5) Treat minor symptoms as early-warning 符.
entries.logic_compare: More minimalist and preventive than encyclopedic yangsheng collections. Less cosmological than 四氣攝生圖, more clinical-practical. Differs from 種芝草法 by focusing on behavior rather than sacred materia.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that 'cultivating perfection' is a secret sequential craft: without ordered steps and concealed keys, scattered longevity tips never cohere into 真. Secrecy protects sequence integrity.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Public miscellaneous tips create false confidence. 2) True work requires staged refinement of body, breath, and spirit. 3) Secrets encode timing, dosage, and contraindications. 4) Wrong order converts medicine to poison. 5) Conclusion: perfection is an engineered process under restricted transmission.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Build a staged curriculum (form → breath → spirit) with clear gates. 2) Hide advanced fire phases until lower gates stabilize. 3) Use BaZi to time stage transitions (e.g., strong Fire years for cautious firing). 4) Keep a private practice log—the modern 祕錄. 5) Test one variable at a time.
entries.logic_compare: More sequential-esoteric than 混俗頤生錄's open lifestyle advice; less single-pointed than 碧虛子直指. Bridges medical yangsheng and full neidan without being pure liturgy.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that health is the art of following the four seasonal qi: each season has a lawful pattern of rise-store-kill-collect, and diagram-mediated knowledge makes that law actionable. Adaptation, not fixed routine, is the method.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Heaven's qi cycles through spring growth, summer flourish, autumn harvest, winter storage. 2) Human body is a microcosm; resisting season creates disease. 3) Diagrams encode clothing, diet, emotion, and exercise per season. 4) Correct seasonal alignment is already 攝生. 5) Conclusion: time-structured living is the primary medicine.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Overlay BaZi month-branch seasons on personal regimen. 2) Spring: move liver-wood (stretch, less anger); winter: store (sleep, less revelation of plans). 3) Use the '圖' idea: one-page seasonal checklist on the wall. 4) Adjust meditation length/heat by season. 5) Read decade luck as a 'long season' and adapt ambition accordingly.
entries.logic_compare: More calendrical-visual than 保生要錄's essential rules, and more secular-medical than stellar 北帝七元 texts. Differs from pure Five-Phase abstract theory by insisting on illustrated, embodied seasonal tactics.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that sacred longevity substances (靈芝) are not only heaven-sent rarities but can be cultivated by correct method—time, terrain, soil, and ritual care. Immortality materia is partly agricultural technology under numinous signs.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Classical longevity lore prizes zhi as condensed auspicious qi. 2) If zhi were purely miraculous, practice would reduce to waiting. 3) Cultivation methods specify conditions that invite zhi growth. 4) Successful growth demonstrates human-heaven cooperation in producing medicine. 5) Conclusion: outer sacred agriculture is a legitimate branch of the path to long life.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat garden/herb work as cultivation of Resource star in BaZi. 2) Align planting and harvest with sexagenary and seasonal qi. 3) Approach materia with purity rules (timing, intention) not only botany. 4) Use 'growing zhi' as metaphor: grow virtues slowly under right conditions. 5) Prefer self-tended simple herbs over exotic untraceable 'immortal drugs'.
entries.logic_compare: Opposite of pure inner 先天一氣 schools that reject outer drugs; more concrete than abstract 願文. Unlike imperial 漢武帝內傳's ready-made peaches of the goddess, this text democratizes the sacred plant through technique—agriculture as minor alchemy.
